transcript.text: The sides of our new fridge freezer get really warm, almost hot, especially near the front edge. Is that a fire risk? It's in an alcove between two units.

No, it is not a fire risk; that warmth is normal because the condenser coils are designed to dissipate heat through the sides. Since yours is new and sits in an alcove, the most likely cause is simply insufficient airflow for the heat to escape into the room. Please make sure there is at least a few centimetres of space between the fridge sides and your units so air can circulate freely. Also, check that it has been running for 24 hours without doors opening often, as new units take time to settle into their temperature.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
Thanks. The gap is only about 1cm each side, with a cupboard above that has a few cm gap. Is that enough? There's no burning smell or scorching, and it's been running fine, it's cooling well.

That 1cm gap is likely too tight for proper air circulation, which explains why the sides are getting so hot. The heat needs space to escape into the room rather than building up against your units. Please try pulling the fridge out slightly to increase that side clearance and see if the warmth reduces after a few hours. Since it is cooling well and there is no burning smell, this sounds like an installation issue rather than a fault with the appliance itself.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I'd rather not pull it out, we've just had the new floor laid and I'm worried about scratching it. Is there another way to sort this? The manual says to leave space but I didn't check exactly how much.

The most practical way to sort this without moving the fridge is to improve the airflow around it or reduce the heat load inside. Since you are worried about scratching the floor, you could try placing a thin, heat-resistant mat under the feet to protect the surface while allowing some air circulation underneath. You might also check if the temperature settings have been adjusted too low recently, as this makes the compressor work harder and generate more side heat. If possible, ensure that no food items are blocking the internal vents, as restricted airflow can sometimes make the unit run hotter than usual.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
The display shows 4C and -18C, so I don't think the settings are too low. I'm not sure a mat under the feet would help, though. Is there anything else I can do without moving the fridge?

Since you cannot move it to increase side clearance, the next most likely cause is internal heat buildup from how much food you have packed inside or where it is placed. If the fridge is very full or if warm food was recently put in, the compressor will run longer and generate more heat on the sides. You can try checking that the internal vents are not blocked by food items, as this restricts airflow and makes the unit work harder. Also, ensure you are not leaving the door open for long periods, which lets hot air in and forces the cooling system to run continuously.
I haven't overfilled it and the doors aren't left open, so I don't think that's it. Is the warmth on the sides actually a problem if it's cooling fine and I can keep my hand on it?

No, it is not a problem if you can keep your hand on it and the appliance is cooling well; that warmth is normal because the condenser coils are designed to dissipate heat through the sides. Since yours is new and sits in an alcove, the most likely cause is simply insufficient airflow for the heat to escape into the room. Please make sure there is at least a few centimetres of space between the fridge sides and your units so air can circulate freely. Also, check that it has been running for 24 hours without doors opening often, as new units take time to settle into their temperature.
